When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index 1/10 (calm, 1-2 signals monitoring) vs VIX Spike Tier 4/4 EXTREME (85% probability, skew active, backwardation active, adaptive active)
The crash index reads price-level signals: drawdowns, breadth, momentum breaks. The VIX Spike Detector reads options market structure. Both can be simultaneously correct because cash prices and options markets price different things on different time horizons. Trust the VIX structure here because all three sub-signals are active at once, and that triple confirmation rarely fires on noise.
⚠ These two disagree: Regime State 8/10 (STABLE, quiet bias) vs Macro Regime TRANSITIONAL at 25% confidence
The Regime State reads price-level trend signals; the Macro Regime reads broader factor alignment across the economy. A 25% confidence reading means the macro detector can't find a clean state, not that conditions are deteriorating sharply. Trust the Regime State for near-term positioning and treat the TRANSITIONAL macro read as a flag to reduce conviction sizing.
Today's tension
The options market is pricing extreme vol expansion while cash prices sit in a low-crash, stable-regime tape.
Bull
The Crash Index reads **1/10** and the Regime State scores **8/10** stable. All three major confluence tripwires are off. Price has not confirmed what options are pricing.
Bear

The tell: Whether HYG (credit) or small-cap drawdown (B2) confirm what the VIX structure is pricing. Both confluences are dark today. If either lights, the vol expansion argument gets independent confirmation from a second market.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The dashboard is delivering a split reading, and the split is genuine. Price-level signals are calm: Crash Index at 1/10, Regime State at 8/10 stable, Contrarian at 31 neutral, zero confluences firing. The options market has simultaneously hit its ceiling: VIX Spike Tier 4/4 with 85% probability and every sub-signal lit. The macro regime is calling a transition at only 25% confidence, which means the underlying factor inputs are mixed rather than cleanly aligned in any direction. You're in a market where the surface is placid and the structure underneath is not.

For positioning, this setup argues for staying exposed but keeping hedges cheap and short-dated. The calm Crash Index and stable Regime State say there's no reason to de-risk on price signals. The VIX backwardation and active skew say the cost of being unhedged is rising, even if price hasn't moved. Neither side is clean enough to carry large net directional conviction, and the 25% macro confidence score reinforces that: the regime detector is telling you to size conservatively until the picture resolves.

The read flips decisively bearish the moment a confluence closes. HYG credit stress or B2 small-cap drawdown confirming alongside VIX backwardation changes the picture entirely. Until then, the divergence between options structure and price action is a warning to hold current exposure rather than add, and the single data point that would end the debate is the T1xHYG confluence lighting.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The macro regime is flagged TRANSITIONAL at 25% confidence. A 25% confidence reading means the underlying factor inputs are mixed, and the model can't cleanly assign the economy to any single state.

This is not a breakdown signal. The Regime State's 8/10 stable score and the Contrarian's 31 neutral score both say the current price environment lacks the extremes that precede clean directional moves.

You're in a blurry middle ground: not late-cycle distress, not early-cycle expansion, not a clean momentum setup, not a classic contrarian reversal. The practical implication is to size conservatively and wait for the regime read to resolve, because a transition that closes into a clear bearish state with confirming confluences calls for a completely different playbook than one that fades back to stable.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence, in plain terms, means assets that historically moved together have started moving apart. Their correlation (the statistical measure of how closely they track each other) drifts away from its prior value. The system tracks 43 such pairs, and 44% of them are currently pulling in different directions. Of those diverging pairs, 17 are breaking in a bearish direction versus only 2 in a bullish direction, a net bias of 15 to the bear side. The mother composite scores 100, a maximum reading, even as the overall composite zone is labeled CALM. That combination means: correlation relationships are breaking down at an extreme rate, the direction of the break is overwhelmingly bearish, but the absolute price moves haven't yet crossed the threshold the system treats as alarming.

The sharpest pair is SPY versus RSP. SPY is the cap-weighted S&P 500 where the five largest names dominate the return. RSP is the equal-weight version where every stock counts equally. Their correlation has drifted from +0.31 to -0.22, meaning they are now moving in opposite directions. A handful of large-cap stocks are pulling the index up while most of the market is not participating. Momentum (MTUM) has decoupled from SPY at +0.42 to -0.24: the stocks that led are no longer carrying the index. Regional banks (KRE) have broken from broad financials (XLF) at +0.11 to -0.50, pointing to stress below the surface of the financial sector that XLF's larger holdings are masking. Visa and Mastercard, nearly identical payment-processing businesses, have reached +0.08 to -0.45 correlation, a degree of separation that usually reflects event-driven positioning in one or both. Value (VTV) and growth (VUG), once moving inversely at -0.35, are now loosely correlated at +0.15, which says factor leadership has blurred. The index is being held together by concentration while the internal market fractures.

Confluences — most proven alpha of the framework 0/3 ACTIVE
AI read · what the confluences mean now

All three major stress confluences are dark today. VIX backwardation is active at the Spike Detector level, but it has not connected with credit stress (HYG), small-cap drawdown (B2), or yen safe-haven inflows.

That gap matters. The options market is paying for protection, but the macro circuits that would confirm a stress regime haven't closed.

A single signal firing in isolation carries less weight than two or three closing simultaneously, because independent markets confirming the same read is what separates a durable stress regime from a positioning squeeze in one instrument. The actionable watch is HYG.

If credit spreads start moving in the same direction as VIX backwardation, the T1xHYG confluence lights and the options market's signal gets independent confirmation from the credit market. Until that happens, the vol signal stands alone.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Korea's KOSPI is the sharpest signal in the global scan, down -4.8% over five days against Asia's leader, the ASX200, at -0.2%. A gap of that magnitude in a semiconductor and export-cycle heavy index is not a local story.

It points to demand or supply-chain deterioration that Seoul is pricing before it shows up in US earnings. In Europe, the DAX is down -1.4% over five days while the Swiss SMI is up +0.1%: a cyclically exposed export index underperforming a defensive, domestically sheltered one is a growth-concern signal for the euro area.

In the US, NDX leads at +0.4% against the Dow's -0.3%, extending the same cap-weight concentration theme visible in the SPY-RSP jaws divergence. The broad market is not participating in the tech lift.

In crypto, BTC is the five-day leader at +2.6% while SOL is flat at +0.0%, which says digital-asset risk appetite is concentrating in the senior store-of-value rather than spreading to higher-beta alternatives. Across all four regions, the pattern is the same: defensives and the most liquid, largest assets hold while cyclicals and smaller, riskier assets lag.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 1/10 and the VIX Spike Detector at Tier 4/4 are reading two separate markets, and both readings are correct at the same time. The Crash Index tracks what price has already done: drawdowns off highs, momentum breaks, breadth collapses.

At 1/10, none of those have happened. The VIX Spike Detector tracks what sophisticated options desks are paying for right now: near-term protection (backwardation means the front-month vol contract costs more than the deferred one), downside tail coverage (skew active), and a cross-signal adaptive confirmation.

All three are simultaneously lit at 85% probability. When cash prices are calm and options structure is priced for stress, the options market is usually early rather than wrong.

Price calm tells you there's no crash in progress. Active VIX structure at the maximum tier tells you the market is paying to price one coming.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.
Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
